conviction_note: Each finding sized on its own, the sum is +1.9. The scaled number is p_up 56 times abs 5.5, which gives +0.66. The two numbers differ because the drivers are mixed. On the positive side: consensus is stale and low ($0.10-0.11 EPS against a likely ~$0.30 headline including a ~$27m vessel gain), Q4 bookings will roughly double Q3's $54k/day, and short interest is building (9.3%) into a beaten-down chart. On the negative side: NAT's own realised rates are a fraction of its peers', those peers' record Q4 bookings were sold or bought only mildly, spot is >60% off the October peak, and NAT's own prints have moved only about 1-7% in both directions.

Chartmill shows $0.18 / $74.98m (snippet only), so the bar is two agreeing sources with one outlier. There is no company numeric guide, only booked days. print_vs_bar_pct is on revenue: my ~$80-88m estimate (16 ships, 75% booked at $54k plus spot) against $69.3m, discounted for the uncertainty about which revenue definition the consensus uses.

expectations.real_bar: For the stock to rise, the Q4 booking disclosure has to show a blended fleet rate clearly above ~$100k/day (roughly double Q3's $54k), with the Q3 dividend at or above Q2's $0.27 and language that the dividend steps up for Q4. A headline EPS beat against a $0.10 consensus is the base case and will not do it alone.

next_guide.street_next_quarter: Not found directly. Derived: FY2026 consensus EPS $0.86 (Global Mosaic, 2026-11-27) less H1 actual $0.54 less Q3 consensus ~$0.10-0.11 implies ~$0.21 for Q4.
next_guide.street_full_year: FY2026 EPS $0.86, EBITDA $256m; FY2027 EPS $0.89 (consensus as quoted by https://theglobalmosaic.substack.com/p/when-the-tankers-arrive)
next_guide.company_current_guide: None numeric. Q3: 'about 75% of our fleet booked at about $54,000 per day per ship' (Q2 6-K, 2026-08-27). Q4: the 2026-11-09 letter says the last 10 spot fixtures averaged ~$144k/day TCE (mostly Q4), with ~50% of the fleet in spot and the rest on 'solid charters'.
next_guide.basis: Q4 bookings will be disclosed as % booked at $/day. With half the fleet fixing spot at ~$144k and the other half on time charters (one May fixture ran 300 days at ~$75k), the blended rate likely lands around $90-110k/day. That is well above Q3's $54k and above what a $0.86 FY consensus implies, but below the short note's $1.00 Q4 EPS and far below peers' Q4 Suezmax books ($272k-$411k).

findings.finding: Q4 2026 booking disclosure: the CEO letter of 2026-11-09 says NAT's last 10 spot fixtures averaged ~60 days at ~$144,000/day TCE (range $59k-$347k), mostly for Q4 2026, with about 50% of the fleet in spot and the rest on 'solid charters'. The Q4 booked rate in the release should therefore be roughly $90-110k/day blended, against Q3's 75% at ~$54k/day. That implies Q4 EPS of perhaps $0.40-0.55 against a street H2 implicitly near $0.32 in total.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: On Q1 2026 (2026-05-28) NAT disclosed Q2 booked 90% at $68k/day, up from Q1's $47.6k, and raised the dividend; the stock fell 3.4%. On Q2 2026 (2026-08-27) it disclosed Q3 booked 75% at $54k, down from $63k, and the stock rose 3.7%. The booking line has not reliably paid in the direction of the number.
findings.why_not_priced: The $144k is public but covers only the spot half, and the time-charter half's rate is not disclosed. The stock is flat since the letter (6.50 on 11-09, 6.45 on 11-27) and consensus FY EPS of $0.86 was not raised to reflect it. If the step-up were priced, sell-side H2 would sit near the buy-side's $1.00+ for Q4 rather than ~$0.32 for H2.
findings.independence: The same document as the mid-quarter finding below, which covers the dividend language; this finding covers only the rate. Different sources pointing the same way: Kpler expects Suezmax rates to 'remain firm through year-end' (https://www.kpler.com/blog/geopolitics-keeps-freight-afloat, 2026-11-06), and the Teekay Q4-to-date Suezmax book is $272k on 63% (https://ca.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/teekay-tankers-q3-2026-slides-record-q4-rates-drive-historic-results-93CH-4953819).

findings.finding: Q3 underlying result likely clears a stale consensus: with 75% of days booked at ~$54k/day (Q2 6-K) and the rest at spot (NAT's own Sept-15 fixtures ran $60k-$200k), the blended Q3 TCE is ~$58-65k on ~16 ships. That gives net voyage revenue of ~$80-88m and underlying EPS of ~$0.18-0.22, before the vessel gain, against a $0.10-0.11 EPS / $69.3m revenue consensus.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 EPS $0.32 against $0.25 (a beat) was followed by +3.7%. Q1 2026 EPS $0.15 against $0.18 (Benzinga basis) by -3.4%. On this name the beat/miss has carried a ~3-4% move.
findings.why_not_priced: The bar is computable by anyone, so it is largely the base case. Only 2-3 analysts cover the name and the consensus was last moved in October, so a headline beat will print on aggregators. Against this, Q2's booking (90% at $68k) realised only $63k including insurance, so NAT realisations have come in below bookings, and Q3 is a step down from Q2 on the reported TCE.
findings.independence: Fixture levels in the 2026-09-15 letter (https://finviz.com/news/392201/nordic-american-tankers-ltd-nyse-nat-exceptional-conditions-for-our-vessels). Even the short report models Q3 EPS at $0.29, above consensus (https://theglobalmosaic.substack.com/p/when-the-tankers-arrive).

findings.finding: Q3 should carry a ~$25-27m gain on the 2005-built Suezmax sold for ~$40m (announced 2026-03-17). It was carried as held for sale at $12.8m at 30 June and delivered in Q3, worth ~$0.12/share on 211.75m shares. Headline EPS likely ~$0.30+ against a $0.10-0.11 consensus.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 carried a $21.3m disposal gain and a headline beat ($0.32 against $0.25); the stock rose 3.7%. Q1 2026 carried a $14.4m gain and the stock fell 3.4%. The gains have not decided the reaction.
findings.why_not_priced: Sale proceeds are not recurring, and the only path to value is the dividend (NAT pays out ~90% of free cash flow to equity). Consensus at $0.10 does not appear to include the gain, so headline-scraping may print an outsized 'beat'. Sized at a fraction because it is below the recurring line.
findings.independence: Held-for-sale balance of $12.845m and 'delivered in Q3' from the Q2 6-K exhibit (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1000177/000091957426005786/p15060137_ex-1.htm).

findings.finding: Peers that already reported Q3 show NAT's realised rates far below the market. Okeanis: Q3 Suezmax $166.6k/day and Q4 60% booked at $410.9k (2026-11-11). Teekay: Q3 Suezmax spot $106.4k and Q4 63% at $272k (2026-11-12). NAT: Q3 ~75% at $54k, and its spot-only Q4 fixtures at ~$144k. Peers' record Q4 books were met with TNK -3.06% and DHT only +1.8%.
findings.link: Same asset class and the same Suezmax spot market: NAT is a 16-17 ship Suezmax pure-play, Okeanis runs Suezmax and VLCC, and Teekay is mostly Suezmax/Aframax. The difference is NAT's older fleet (~11 years) and ~50% time-charter cover.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Peers on their Q3 2026 prints: TNK -3.06% after record Q4 bookings, DHT +1.8% after 68% of VLCC Q4 spot days booked at $579.9k and a $1.45 dividend. The sector has been selling record forward books.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: NAT underperformed DHT/TNK by ~7 points over 20 sessions and trades at 0.79x NAV. A NAT Q4 number at ~$100k set beside peers' $270-410k may still read as a laggard on the day.
findings.independence: Teekay slides (https://ca.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/teekay-tankers-q3-2026-slides-record-q4-rates-drive-historic-results-93CH-4953819, 2026-11-12). DHT reaction (https://www.bairdmaritime.com/shipping/tankers/dht-holdings-third-quarter-profit). findings.finding: Shorts are building into the print: 16.20M (10-15) to 17.48M (10-30) to 19.69M shares short (11-13), 9.3% of shares and ~4 days to cover. A public short thesis dated 2026-11-27 names the 30 Nov results as its catalyst, and its own model already has Q3 EPS $0.29 and Q4 EPS $1.00.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior NAT print with short interest at this level was observed in the sources. Short interest peaked at 21.9M in June 2026 per the short report, and the stock ran from 5.15 (06-11) to 6.46 (06-23) in that period (Hormuz-driven).
findings.why_not_priced: A crowded, rising short with ~4 days to cover is a squeeze mechanism on a strong Q4 book. The short thesis is long-dated (2027-28 newbuild deliveries) and its stated carry cost is the dividend, so a high Q3 dividend declaration hurts the short carry within the window.
findings.independence: The short report itself (https://theglobalmosaic.substack.com/p/when-the-tankers-arrive) quotes 19.7M short, 9.9% of float. ShortSqueeze showed 16.2M and 3.7 days on 2026-11-11 (sweep row).

findings.finding: Q3 dividend risk: Q2's $0.27 ($57.2m) was paid out of quarterly adjusted EBITDA of $67.6m, which included $14.6m of loss-of-hire insurance. Q3 recurring cash earnings, at a ~$54-65k TCE and without that insurance, look similar or lower, so the Q3 dividend may be flat to slightly down ($0.22-0.30) while peers pay record sums (DHT $1.45, ECO $7.00).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Dividend raised $0.17 to $0.22 at Q1: stock -3.4%. Raised $0.22 to $0.27 at Q2: +3.7%. Raised to $0.17 at Q4 2025: +7.1%. No observed cut in 2026.
findings.why_not_priced: Yield screens price NAT on the $1.61/12-month figure the short report expects, which is back-loaded into Q4. A flat Q3 dividend with no Q4 signal would read as a cut relative to the sector. The CEO's 'healthy dividends' (11-09) leaves room either way, and NAT might fold the ~$40m sale proceeds into the payout, which is the upside.
findings.independence: CEO's 'NAT will continue to pay healthy dividends' (https://finviz.com/news/419139/nordic-american-tankers-ltd-nyse-nat-the-tanker-bonanza-continues) points the other way. Peer dividends from the DHT and Okeanis releases.

findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: the letters are public and promotional. The residual is that management has committed in writing to 'historically high' contract levels for Q4, so a weak Q4 book would contradict its own statements, which makes that outcome less likely.

The Sep-15 letter (https://finviz.com/news/392201/nordic-american-tankers-ltd-nyse-nat-exceptional-conditions-for-our-vessels) and Sep-23 letter (https://finviz.com/news/394541/nordic-american-tankers-ltd-nyse-nat-the-direction-is-up). It shares the Nov-09 document with the next-guide finding; the rate is counted there, the dividend wording is the dividend finding's counterweight.

findings.why_not_priced: It is a macro proxy, mostly in sector prices. It matters only as weekend headline risk into a Monday print.

baseline_tension: The baseline's 20-day -20.5% and absent skew leave room for a positive reaction, and my lean agrees with a mean-reversion read off a low bar. The weight against it is that NAT's prints have moved only ~1-7% in either direction and peers sold their record Q4 books, so p_up stays close to 50.
lessons_applied: Rule 2 (one-offs): vessel-sale gain cut from +0.5 to +0.3; it has no stated path to guidance, only to the dividend.
Rule 1 (verified fact is not a reaction): Q3 consensus-beat finding cut from +0.6 to +0.4, because NAT fell 3.4% after a Q1 dividend raise and peers sold record Q4 books.
Rule 7 (crowded short shrinks negatives): peer-discount finding cut from -0.8 to -0.6 and dividend-risk finding from -0.4 to -0.3, with short interest at 9.3% and rising.
Rule 6 (verify the bar): bar sourced to two agreeing estimates ($0.10 EW, $0.11 Benzinga) with a $0.18 outlier noted; sizes on bar-dependent findings kept small.
Base-rate lesson for foreign private issuers: rebuilt the reaction history from the four confirmed results releases instead of the baseline's 6-K matches; abs_move left at 5.5.

The mid-quarter-statements finding (+0.2) was filed at write-up to meet the v3b addendum's section 3, not because of this file; it was not in the frozen draft (10 findings, sum +1.8). Post-lessons p_up moved from 55 to 56 because the rebuilt reaction history showed no persistent selling of NAT prints. Final sum +1.9.
